# Danny Ahn — dannyahn.com

Danny Ahn is an AI data systems architect based in Las Vegas / Henderson, Nevada — with 20+ years across MIS and IT: computer software & hardware repair, and managing software systems for education, real estate, and small business. He builds intelligent, secure, scalable AI infrastructure on top of that foundation.

## Core Expertise
- Artificial Intelligence: machine learning systems, intelligent data pipelines, AI-driven security — turning models into production infrastructure (currently running Qwen 3.6 35B A3B at 256k context on a quad RTX 3060 build)
- MIS & IT: computer software and hardware repair; managing software systems for education, real estate, and small business
- Cybersecurity: threat analysis, vulnerability assessment, zero trust architecture
- Cloud Infrastructure: cloud-native design and deployment at scale
- Data Systems: pipeline architecture, database design for high-concurrency workloads (sharding, replication, consistency models)
- DevOps & Automation: production-grade Terraform/IaC, state management, CI/CD integration

## Career Highlights
- Pre-2012 — Two decades of hands-on MIS and IT: software & hardware repair; managing software systems for education, real estate, and small business
- 2012 — Analyzed MGM Mirage's casino player club database and loyalty program infrastructure; identified vulnerabilities in enterprise data systems
- 2015+ — Enterprise cybersecurity with Fortune 500 companies: threat analysis and security architecture
- 2018+ — Cloud & infrastructure leadership for mid-market organizations
- 2021+ — AI-focused practice: applying machine learning to enterprise security, cloud infrastructure, and data systems

## Featured Guide
"What is an AI data systems architect?" — the full answer lives at https://dannyahn.com/ai-data-systems-architect.html. An AI data systems architect designs and oversees the end-to-end infrastructure that lets artificial intelligence run in production: machine learning pipelines, model serving platforms, real-time data foundations, cloud architecture, and the security controls that tie them together.
